A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same future frame synthesis survey. The text, equations, table, and figure support comparison. The dataset and application material in v4's appendix is incorporated into v5 Sections 2.2 and 6.

before.justification: Table 1 reports dataset means and medians, but v4 does not establish whether the authors calculated these statistics or obtained them from cited sources. No original model experiments are reported; attribution of the descriptive data analysis remains unclear.

after.justification: Section 2.2 explicitly states that the authors calculate mean or median dataset statistics when source papers or project pages lack details. Together with the reported statistics in Table 1, this supports original descriptive data analysis, although no original model experiments are reported.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new synthesis algorithm. The additional transformer discussion in v5 Section 3.1.4 reviews existing methods rather than changing a proposed architecture, objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Table 1 retains the same video datasets. Newly discussed image datasets and applications, including anomaly detection, expand literature coverage rather than datasets or tasks actually used in the authors' training or evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed system. Newly discussed methods such as CAIN, FLAVR, and PEEKABOO are literature additions, not additional experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The expanded discussion of metrics, data filtering, and resolution in v5 provides criticism and recommendations. It does not introduce or revise executed training or evaluation protocols, splits, budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or diagnostic case studies. The added Challenges passages provide interpretive criticism rather than new supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its mean and median reporting conventions. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests are introduced. The new explanation identifies the provenance of missing-source statistics without changing the reported statistical practice.

E6.justification: Table 1's dataset statistics are unchanged. However, v5 Section 3.1.1 newly reports an efficiency finding attributed to OpenSTL: recurrent models have higher FLOPs and lower FPS than recurrent-free models. This adds a cited empirical finding absent from v4 Section 4.1, rather than a new author-conducted benchmark.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 preserves both problem-formulation equations, including conditioning on auxiliary information and control signals. Neither version contains theorems or proofs. The added qualitative limitations do not revise formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The central stochasticity-based taxonomy and survey focus remain. However, v4 Section 7 recommends moving away from lightweight models, whereas v5 Section 8 explicitly supports both lightweight short-term applications and resource-intensive generative models, narrowing the earlier general recommendation.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands substantive criticism across Sections 2–6. It questions whether visual quality measures world-model usefulness, explains why better optical-flow accuracy can yield worse synthesis, and adds specific limitations concerning scaling, disentanglement, controllability, and application transfer. This goes well beyond v4's broader challenge overview and selected caveats.

D1.justification: v5 Section 2.2 newly explains that the authors calculate means or medians when dataset details are unavailable in the sources. v4 identifies these statistic types in Table 1 without explaining their provenance. This clarifies construction of the existing table without establishing recomputation.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands the reviewed literature, including deterministic transformer and interpolation methods, image-data resources, and additional applications. New Section 7 discusses previous surveys and OpenSTL in detail and clarifies the survey's positioning, extending v4's brief introductory comparisons.

P1.justification: The abstract and roadmap are rewritten, diffusion and token-generation discussions are regrouped under descriptive headings, and appendix material enters the main narrative. The standalone Future Research section is absorbed into the conclusion, while a dedicated Related Work section is introduced. These substantially change the document's organization.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one with a redesigned title and author block. v4's taxonomy diagram, Figure 1, is removed. Table 1 moves from the appendix to the background section and loses its dedicated Year column while retaining its dataset statistics.

improvement.justification: v5 provides more useful method-specific criticism and clearer positioning against previous surveys. Its revised conclusion better reconciles practical efficiency with ambitious generative modeling. These improve the survey's analytical value, although removal of the taxonomy diagram and repetition in several Challenges passages limit the overall gain.
